title: Prove mask attribution from invariant one- and two-dimensional caller blocks
body:
A common invariant flag with one- and two-dimensional quotients suffices for mask-only attribution in characteristic zero. Trace and determinant handle noncommuting two-dimensional blocks. A literal example separates strict support from mask attribution.

## Scope and source

Uses the #7903 incidence projectors. The strict separator has even q targets and no HOSTs; the full tight RC2 case remains open. DreamingOfClouds’ Q=0 and thin toolkit extension is #7869 at `06c207a9feb3994a4b987dc3010657b6e85b7956`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-qzero-invariant-blocks/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 verify.py` passed with SymPy, including four-root word checks, regenerated witnesses, and full matrix-algebra certificates for three original small callers. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Seek a mask-only transfer for irreducible quotients of dimension at least three. All three published small-word controls are already irreducible.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
